Integrate the Nuro Driver with new vehicle platforms via CAN and Ethernet interfaces to OEM ECUs

strengths: Register-level bare-metal C driver development on Cortex-M4 — STM32 Temperature Monitor programs GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 directly, with a hand-written low-level I2C driver, timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM. This is the JD's 'device driver development' depth option, backed concretely rather than by keyword.
RTOS task coordination with synchronization primitives — Object Tracking Turret uses FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory coordination alongside interrupt-driven UART and multi-servo PWM.

Actuator interface work across three independent projects — multi-servo PWM (turret), four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM via Cytron drivers with angle-weighted joystick-to-wheel mixing (Robocon), two-link IK driving five servos (COFFIN). The JD names 'actuator interface' as an application component and this is directly it.

Safe-state / fault handling implemented from first principles — Robocon's fail-safe state machine halts all motors on controller disconnect; COFFIN's gripper ToF range-gate closes at 25 mm for contact-aware grasping. Both are the pattern behind 'bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.'

Hands-on hardware-vs-software debugging, which the JD calls out explicitly — COFFIN resolved 11 integration failures including servo brown-out, stale-frame capture and false-positive detections; Planctech resolved accelerometer jitter via software calibration and resolution tuning.
Interrupt-driven peripheral work written from scratch — a 4-bit A/B quadrature transition state machine on hardware interrupts (Robocon), not a vendor HAL call.

Concurrency and CS fundamentals with measured results — MPI Hodgkin-Huxley (10.49x speedup, 65% degradation characterized under load imbalance) and four work-distribution strategies benchmarked on a parallel ray tracer (30x).
Closed-loop control evidence for the vehicle-dynamics bonus — encoder-odometry heading correction feeding angular error back into rotation PWM, plus visual servoing in COFFIN.
Cross-discipline collaboration at the scale the JD describes — led a 25-member robotics team owning mechanical, PCB and ML integration; took over as team lead of 7 mid-project at Teesside.
real_gaps: CAN bus — not one bullet in the entire profile mentions CAN, in any form. The JD names it in the required qualifications, again in the depth-in-at-least-one list, again in the bench-tools line (CAN tools), and again in the bonus section (DBC).

Automotive and vehicle domain entirely absent — no vehicle platform, no OEM or ECU interface, no supplier engagement, no production launch. CARLA autonomous driving is a simulator-side perception and control stack, not vehicle integration; it never touches a real actuator, a real bus or a real power-on.
ISO 26262 and functional safety — no evidence of safety requirement derivation, hazard analysis, requirements traceability, or any regulated development process (no DO-178C or IEC 62304 either).

Automated verification infrastructure — no unit-test framework, no test automation, no CI for firmware anywhere in the profile. Validation is manual trial counting (10/10 picks, <2 mm over 10 trials). The JD asks the hire to build and maintain unit tests and HIL benches.
Hardware-in-the-loop benches — bench bring-up exists, but no HIL rig, no simulated-plant testing.
Bootloader, software update and secure boot — nothing, including no flash partitioning or A/B update work.
Multicore microcontroller programming — MPI and CUDA are host-side multi-process and GPU parallelism, not AMP/lockstep core management, inter-core communication or core-affinity scheduling on an MCU.
AUTOSAR Classic, MCAL, Infineon AURIX TC3xx, SafeRTOS — no exposure to any automotive base-software stack or automotive silicon.
Vehicle network tooling — DBC, ARXML, UDS diagnostics, E2E protection, time synchronization (PTP/gPTP) all absent.
Power distribution and monitoring at vehicle level — ADC sensing exists, but no power-rail management, no load distribution, no brown-out detection beyond having debugged one servo brown-out.

Seniority, as prose and not scored here: 0 years full-time against a 3+ year industry requirement and a Senior title, with seven internships standing in. The JD's 'hiring across levels' line softens this, but every experience entry is research, ML or student-club work — only Planctech is an embedded internship, and it is a gesture-glove prototype.
overstated_by_keywords: 'unit testing' was counted as Have — there is no test-automation evidence anywhere in the profile. This should have been Missing.
'RTOS' — real but shallow for this role. One project uses FreeRTOS mutexes; the JD wants someone extending the RTOS, scheduler and base software itself.

'automotive Ethernet -> TCP/IP sockets' — the adjacency is thin. COFFIN's WebSocket fabric is application-layer Python over Flask-SocketIO on Linux hosts; automotive Ethernet means SOME/IP, AVB/TSN and MAC-level work on an MCU.

'hardware debugging (oscilloscope, logic analyzer)' — these are listed in the skills block but no bullet shows an instrument used to find a specific defect. The JD treats bench instrumentation as daily work.
'hardware-in-the-loop bench -> bench bring-up' — bring-up is real, HIL is not. These are different activities.
'concurrency' — strong as HPC/distributed concurrency, much weaker as the embedded task concurrency and shared-state discipline the JD means.
understated_by_keywords: Actuator interface and body controls were both marked Missing, yet servo and motor command paths appear in three separate projects with PWM frequencies, driver ICs and mixing math specified. This is the closest thing in the profile to the JD's application-component work.
Fault management was marked Missing, but the Robocon controller-disconnect fail-safe state machine and COFFIN's ToF range-gate are exactly safe-state transitions on fault detection.

Device driver development scored as a generic keyword match, understating it — the STM32 monitor is register-level peripheral bring-up with a hand-rolled I2C driver and measured flash/RAM footprint, which is unusually concrete for a new-grad profile.
The JD's explicit 'you enjoy finding out why hardware and software disagree' has no keyword, but COFFIN's 11 documented integration failures answer it better than most of the matched terms do.
screening_gaps: Zero CAN bus experience. The JD names CAN four separate times — required qualifications, the depth-in-at-least-one list, the bench-tools line, and the DBC bonus. For a team whose job is the controllers between the autonomy stack and the vehicle, a resume with no CAN on it does not survive the first read.

No automotive or vehicle experience of any kind, against a Senior title and a 3+ year industry requirement with 0 years full-time. The team's work is OEM ECU integration and vehicle bring-up on public roads; nothing in the profile shows a real vehicle, a real bus, or a shipped product.

No functional-safety or regulated-process development. The JD puts ISO 26262 requirement derivation and full traceability in the core work, not the bonus section, and there is no safety-process or automated-verification evidence to point at.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The generic embedded half of this role is genuinely backed — register-level C drivers on Cortex-M4, RTOS mutex coordination, interrupt-driven peripheral work written from scratch, servo and motor command paths, and real hardware-vs-software debugging with documented failures. The automotive half, which is the actual spine of the job, is unevidenced end to end: no CAN, no vehicle, no OEM interface, no ISO 26262, no bootloader, no automotive base software, and no automated verification infrastructure. Keyword scoring and this read land close together here (delta under 5 points, against a historical +30), which means the 47.8% is not keyword inflation — it is an accurate picture of a candidate who has the embedded fundamentals and none of the domain.
